name: Terminal (macOS)
summary: Apple's built-in macOS Terminal. Appearance lives in profiles (.terminal property lists) with ANSI colors, font, cursor, translucency with blur and a background image. No ligatures, padding, shaders, images or quake mode. Profile files hold NSKeyedArchiver blobs for colors and fonts, so they are generated with plutil rather than typed.

macos.notes: Preinstalled; nothing to install. Profiles are NOT separate files on disk: they are dictionaries under 'Window Settings' in ~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.Terminal.plist (a binary plist managed by cfprefsd; do not edit it while Terminal runs). The supported way to add a profile is a .terminal file (an XML plist) imported with Terminal > Settings > Profiles > Action > Import, drag-and-drop onto the profile list (both in the Apple Terminal User Guide), or `open file.terminal` (works in practice per community reports; not in Apple's docs). Scriptable with `defaults` (default and startup profile names) and plutil (build the .terminal file). Colors and fonts inside a profile are base64 NSKeyedArchiver blobs, built with plutil as shown in the palette and font recipes. Apple does not document the profile key names; the ones used here come from exported .terminal files and community dumps, and are flagged where unverified. Safest check after any scripted change: look at the result in Terminal > Settings > Profiles.

ligatures.notes: The User Guide's Text settings list no ligature option. Use iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm or Ghostty.

font-fallback.notes: No fallback list; macOS substitutes fonts per glyph. Use a Nerd Font as the main font for icons.

background-animated.notes: Static images only. Use kitty, Ghostty or WezTerm.

shader.notes: No shader support. Use Ghostty or kitty.

padding.notes: No padding setting in the User Guide's Text or Window panes. Use iTerm2 (margins) or another terminal.

titlebar.notes: Native title bar only. Profiles > Window > Title chooses what the title shows (working directory, path, process name, dimensions...), not the chrome. For a borderless look use another terminal.

splits.notes: No independent split panes. Terminal has a Shell > Split Pane command, but user reports describe it as a second view of the same session, not a new shell (not confirmed in Apple's docs). Use tabs, tmux or zellij.

quake.notes: No drop-down mode. Use iTerm2's hotkey window.

shell-integration.notes: No configurable shell integration in the User Guide. Terminal sets TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal and macOS's zsh startup tracks the working directory for it (community knowledge, not verified here).

inline-images.notes: No inline image protocol is documented. Use iTerm2, kitty or WezTerm.
